description: "skolotāja" (feminine) is lemmatized to the masculine "skolotājs". In Latvian dictionaries the feminine agent noun is its own lemma ("skolotāja"). The note "fem. nom." confirms this is not an inflected form of "skolotājs" but a distinct feminine lemma. As written, a learner looking up "skolotājs" will find a word Anna does not actually use.
suggestedFix: Set lemma to "skolotāja" and add it to newLemmas/dictionary.json (or explicitly document a course-wide decision to lemmatize m/f pairs under the masculine, with a note like "fem. of skolotājs").

description: "labi" is lemmatized to the adjective "labs" but glossed "well". This violates R13's one-lemma-one-gloss consistency: "labs" as an adjective must gloss "good", so the same lemma would need two glosses without an explicit multi-sense dictionary entry. Latvian dictionaries treat the adverb "labi" as its own lemma.
suggestedFix: Lemmatize as "labi" (adv.) with gloss "well", add "labi" to newLemmas; or explicitly register labs: ["good", "well"] as a multi-sense entry in dictionary.json.

description: The verb "dzīvot" (dzīvoju) is used in the lesson but is missing from newLemmas. Per R13, every new lemma requires a dictionary entry and human review before merge; an undeclared lemma will fail validation and leaves the learner without a dictionary reference.
The question word "kur" is used (and is pedagogically new — R10 material) but is not declared in newLemmas.

The preposition "no" is used but not declared in newLemmas. R8 explicitly requires each preposition's allowed glosses to be enumerated in dictionary.json for the validator; an undeclared preposition cannot be validated.
suggestedFix: Add "no" to newLemmas with the approved gloss list ["from"].

description: Proper noun "Rīga" is not in newLemmas, yet "Latvija" is. The lesson is internally inconsistent about whether proper nouns are declared lemmas.
suggestedFix: Add "Rīga" to newLemmas, or remove "Latvija" and document that proper nouns are exempt.

description: Lesson-level: newLemmas declares eight lemmas that never appear in any sentence: labrīt, vārds, lūdzu, atvainojiet, nākt, tur, ārsts, kā. Declared-but-untaught vocabulary inflates the lesson's apparent coverage and will desynchronize dictionary tracking.
suggestedFix: Either add sentences exercising these lemmas or remove them from newLemmas.

description: Lesson-level: the title promises "Kas tu esi? (Who are you?)" but no sentence contains "kas", any self-introduction, or names ("vārds" is declared but unused, and the speakers Pēteris and Anna never introduce themselves). The title misrepresents the content.
suggestedFix: Either add an introduction exchange (e.g. "Kā tevi sauc?" / "Mans vārds ir Anna") or retitle the lesson to match the actual content (greetings, languages, occupations).

description: "Es mācos latviski" is nonstandard: "mācīties" normally takes an object ("Es mācos latviešu valodu"), while the adverb "latviski" pairs with runāt/saprast/lasīt. A native speaker would find this phrasing off, and A1 material should model the standard construction.
suggestedFix: Change the target to "Es mācos latviešu valodu." (adjusting tokens), or at minimum flag the colloquial status; note this also affects the natural field.

description: "Sveiki" is grammatically plural; addressing a single man, the strictly correct form is "Sveiks" (fem. "Sveika"). "Sveiki" as a universal greeting is common colloquially, but an A1 lesson introducing greetings should either teach the agreement or note the colloquial usage.
suggestedFix: Add a note to the token (e.g. "pl. form, used colloquially as a general greeting") or use "Sveiks".

description: Word order issue: "Man arī patīk lasīt un ceļot" most naturally means "I, too, like reading" (arī scopes over Man — 'me as well'), whereas the natural translation "I also like to read and to travel" implies additional activities, which in Latvian would be "Man patīk arī lasīt un ceļot." In the drill's context (following d1's list of likes), the intended meaning is the latter.
suggestedFix: Change the target to "Man patīk arī lasīt un ceļot." (moving the arī token), or change the natural translation to "I like to read and to travel too."

description: Lesson-level: every sentence has audioApproved: false. Publishing with unapproved audio violates the release standard.
suggestedFix: Complete audio review and set audioApproved: true for all sentences before publication.
